name: Encore Radio
author: Nick Scilingo Nick S(NJ)
description: Keep the radio station feel going after the light show ends. Streams a custom internet radio URL, TuneIn stations, or a folder of music from a network share (free), or Pandora and Spotify playlists (premium), through your after-hours schedule. Source Fallback (auto-recovery if a source fails) is free for every source; Source Rotation (a different source on a day/time schedule) is premium. Includes Announcement Assistant integration for scheduled station-style announcements.

privacy.summary: Streams a station or your shared library (free), or Pandora/Spotify (premium), through FPP. The 10-hour trial is tracked locally and never reported anywhere.

sends.what: Hardware ID + license key when validating; your email if saved, for reminders; for Spotify sign-in, the OAuth code and your device's own local callback address (token exchange itself happens entirely on your device, not the server)
sends.why: license validation, optional email reminders, and unlocking Pandora/Spotify/Rotation

sends.to: TuneIn (opml.radiotime.com and the station's resolved stream host)
sends.what: your TuneIn search text and playback requests

sends.to: the custom stream URL or network share you configure
sends.what: a playback request, or for a network share, the CIFS username/password you configure
sends.why: starting playback of the free source you picked

sends.what: your Spotify account tokens and search/playback requests

sends.to: Pandora's servers (via the bundled pianobar client)
sends.what: your Pandora login and playback requests

sends.to: Spotify's servers (via the bundled Raspotify/librespot service)
sends.what: this device's online status, for Spotify Connect discovery
sends.why: lets your Spotify app find and cast to this device

collects.what: An email or license key - required for Pandora/Spotify/Rotation, never for free sources.
Cumulative premium trial seconds used - local only, resettable by editing this file.
Spotify client ID/secret and access/refresh tokens

collects.where: plugindata/fpp-EncoreRadio/encoreradio.json (mode 600), and in plugindata/fpp-EncoreRadio/netshare_authfile (mode 600) for the duration of playback - removed on Stop

systemChanges.what: Creates and enables encoreradio-pulse.service - on FPP 9.x/no PipeWire this is a system-wide PulseAudio instance and overwrites /etc/pulse/system.pa; on FPP 10.x/PipeWire it instead installs and runs pipewire-pulse (no system.pa involved), joined to FPP's own PipeWire graph
Enables Raspotify (raspotify.service) once Spotify is configured; not started otherwise
Adds the pulse and fpp users to the audio group
Downloads/installs the Raspotify .deb from dtcooper.github.io, checksum-verified via api.github.com when available
Edits /etc/raspotify/conf (audio backend, device name) when Raspotify is installed
Reads a network (SMB) share you configure via smbclient, in small batches, not a kernel filesystem mount; the local relay listens on 127.0.0.1 only

privacy.other: Pandora, Spotify, and Source Rotation are locked until you register an email or already have a license key; Source Fallback and the free sources are never gated. Uninstalling leaves plugindata/fpp-EncoreRadio/ (config, license, trial progress, saved credentials), the raspotify package and /etc/raspotify/conf, and the pulse/fpp audio-group membership in place - reinstalling doesn't lose your settings or need to re-download anything. The PulseAudio/PipeWire-pulse changes above are only reverted when this plugin was the one that created them; if another plugin (e.g. Announcement Assistant) set them up first, uninstalling leaves that alone.
